findings.title: Shard path interpolates queries twice, once here and again inside runSplitQuery
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() now calls applyTemplateVariables on every target (line 52), and splitQueriesByStreamShard() then builds subRequest with those already-interpolated targets. Each subRequest is passed to runSplitQuery(), which calls applyTemplateVariables again on every target (querySplitting.ts line 299). Interpolation is therefore applied twice to the same expression. Any value that contains a '$' or other template-like text after the first pass gets interpolated a second time. The test change that expects applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times reflects this double application rather than a deliberate design. Interpolation should happen in exactly one place for the sharded path.

findings.title: Interpolation before querySupportsSplitting breaks the $__range check
findings.body: querySupportsSplitting() relies on isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) to keep $__range queries from being split. The comment on that check says the range must not be split because $__range is interpolated on the backend against the split time range. Now that applyTemplateVariables runs at line 299, before partition() at line 300, the expr seen by isQueryWithRangeVariable is already interpolated. If the Loki datasource resolves $__range on the frontend, the variable is gone by the time the check runs, so $__range queries would be split and get an incorrect range. The check should run on the original expression, or the test suite should cover a $__range query to confirm the behaviour is preserved.

findings.title: Empty-expression filter runs before interpolation, so a variable that expands to empty is not dropped
findings.body: The filter `.filter((query) => query.expr)` runs at line 298, before applyTemplateVariables at line 299. A target whose expr is a variable that interpolates to an empty string passes the filter and is sent as an empty query. Filtering after interpolation, or filtering both before and after, would avoid this.
